result.note: Tests the proposed FCRA amendment and the Constitution Amendment Bill on removing detained ministers, both before Parliament in the July 2026 Monsoon Session.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the amendment to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) taken up for debate in Parliament's Monsoon Session in July 2026:
items: It cuts the maximum prison sentence for FCRA violations from five years to one year.
It allows a government-appointed authority to control and dispose of foreign contributions, and assets created from them, when an organisation's FCRA registration ends.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The amendment both lowers the maximum prison term to one year and lets a government-appointed authority take over foreign-funded assets once registration ends. The FCRA governs how Indian organisations receive and use overseas donations.
questions.source: The proposed amendment cuts the maximum prison sentence for violations from five years to one.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Constitution Amendment Bill on removing ministers held in custody, as it stood in July 2026:
items: It would apply to the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers as well as other ministers.
It applies to custody over an alleged offence carrying a maximum sentence of at least five years.
The parliamentary committee examining it submitted its final report just before the Monsoon Session opened.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. On 17 July 2026 the committee deferred its report for further consultation, after a draft that proposed suspension in place of removal. The bill would remove ministers, including the PM and CMs, after 30 consecutive days in custody over such an offence.
questions.source: The Constitution Amendment Bill would remove ministers, including the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers, after 30 consecutive days in custody over an alleged offence carrying a maximum sentence of at least five years.
